seed: A shape drawn with the Pen came out at whatever weight the canvas gave it and stayed there: the panel offered its colour, its opacity and its blending and nothing else, while every other shape in the app keeps a Thickness right beside its colour. The walk draws two paths, picks one, and reads the row: it has to be there, read the weight the line actually has, change the line live, land as ONE undo step, reach two paths at once, and let the weight you chose win over the thinner one an icon frame would otherwise hand a fresh Pen.

steps.note: the first of two open paths, out of the Pen at the weight every new line ships with. Both are drawn BEFORE anything is rethickened, because the Pen now keeps the weight you last chose and the row below needs two lines that differ.
the second, at the same weight, and it is the one still picked

THE TEST: picking the drawn path offers a Thickness under its colour row in Appearance, reading the weight the line actually has. Before this the panel offered Opacity, Blending and a colour, and nothing that could change the line.
pulling it took the line from 4 to 9 and the canvas followed it up
ONE undo step puts the whole pull back, however many previews went through it on the way
both paths picked, one 9 and one 4: ONE row, reading Mixed, exactly as a colour row does
one pull reached both: the row stops saying Mixed and both lines land on 3
THE TEST: ONE undo put BOTH lines back. Had it reached only one, the row would read a number rather than Mixed

THE TEST: a path drawn on a 24 pixel icon frame comes out at the 3 that was CHOSEN a moment ago, not the 2 the frame hands a Pen still holding the stock weight. The frame's thinning is a starting value, and it stops the moment you pick a weight of your own. A Pen that had never been rethickened still arrives at 2 here, which is what icon-stroke-weight-walk checks.
